events.subtitle: 90th-birthday program with two U.S. premieres

venue.name: Stern Auditorium / Perelman Stage at Carnegie Hall

priority_review.rationale: A+ understates this specific night: Carnegie Hall is marking Reich's 90th birthday with a one-night program spanning five decades and two U.S. premieres, including a Carnegie co-commission, performed by Bang on a Can All-Stars and Ensemble Signal with longtime/new-generation collaborators. The milestone and premiere concentration make missing this New York performance genuinely regrettable, while the broader international Reich-at-90 season keeps it below alter-plans singularity.

events.factual_description: Carnegie Hall marks Steve Reich's 90th birthday on October 22, 2026 in Stern Auditorium / Perelman Stage with an all-Reich program spanning five decades. Bang on a Can All-Stars and Ensemble Signal join under Brad Lubman. Lisa Kaplan and Nico Muhly perform the U.S. premiere of Two Pianos; the combined ensembles perform the U.S. premiere of In All Your Ways, co-commissioned by Carnegie Hall, alongside Double Sextet and Jacob's Ladder; Bryce Dessner performs Electric Counterpoint. Bang on a Can's official event page lists the concert at 8:00 PM.

en.why_it_matters: This is not a retrospective that happens to land near a birthday. Carnegie is using Reich's 90th to put new work beside the rhythmic architecture that changed contemporary music: two U.S. premieres in the same room, one of them a Carnegie co-commission, with Bang on a Can All-Stars and Ensemble Signal sharing the stage. The point is hearing the vocabulary continue to move, not watching it get embalmed.
en.trip_verdict: Protect this night if a New York trip can be shaped around it. The birthday, premiere concentration and interpreters make a dedicated regional trip defensible; the wider international Reich-at-90 season means there are other ways to encounter the anniversary without blowing up every other plan.

es.why_it_matters: No es una retrospectiva que por casualidad cae cerca de un cumpleaños. Carnegie está usando los 90 años de Reich para poner música nueva junto a la arquitectura rítmica que cambió la música contemporánea: dos estrenos en Estados Unidos en la misma sala, uno de ellos cocomisionado por Carnegie, con Bang on a Can All-Stars y Ensemble Signal compartiendo escenario. La gracia es escuchar cómo ese lenguaje todavía se mueve, no verlo convertido en museo.
es.trip_verdict: Protegería esa noche si se puede armar un viaje a Nueva York alrededor de ella. El aniversario, la concentración de estrenos y los intérpretes sí justifican un viaje regional dedicado; como hay un ciclo internacional amplio por los 90 años de Reich, tampoco hace falta volar todo lo demás del calendario para vivir ese aniversario.

venue.name: Stern Auditorium / Perelman Stage at Carnegie Hall

The exact birthday plus a major new symphonic work makes this a genuine-regret-if-missed New York event, while multiple worldwide Glass-at-90 celebrations keep it short of alter-plans singularity.

events.factual_description: Carnegie Hall presents Philip Glass's 90th-birthday concert on January 31, 2027, the composer's actual 90th birthday, in Stern Auditorium / Perelman Stage. Dennis Russell Davies conducts Orchestra of St. Luke's in 'Mechanical Ballet' from The Voyage, Violin Concerto No. 1 with Robert McDuffie, and the New York premiere of Symphony No. 15 'Lincoln' with baritone Zachary James. Philip Glass's official site announced on August 10 that single tickets are on sale and links to the exact Carnegie Hall event page for a 2:00 PM performance.

en.why_it_matters: The date is doing real musical work here. Glass turns 90 that day, and Carnegie pairs the milestone with a New York premiere rather than treating the evening as a greatest-hits tribute. Dennis Russell Davies, Robert McDuffie and Orchestra of St. Luke's are not decorative names around the composer; they are interpreters with deep ties to his orchestral language. The night looks backward and forward at the same time.
en.trip_verdict: Protect the afternoon if a New York trip can be built around it. The exact birthday, the Lincoln symphony's New York premiere and the collaborator lineage justify a dedicated regional trip; Glass is being celebrated worldwide at 90, so this remains one major node in a larger anniversary rather than the only possible encounter.

es.why_it_matters: Aquí la fecha sí hace trabajo musical. Glass cumple 90 años ese mismo día y Carnegie liga el aniversario a un estreno neoyorquino en vez de convertir la tarde en un repaso de grandes éxitos. Dennis Russell Davies, Robert McDuffie y la Orchestra of St. Luke’s no son nombres decorativos alrededor del compositor: tienen una relación profunda con su lenguaje orquestal. La función mira hacia atrás y hacia adelante al mismo tiempo.
es.trip_verdict: Protegería la tarde si se puede construir un viaje a Nueva York alrededor de ella. El cumpleaños exacto, el estreno neoyorquino de la sinfonía Lincoln y el linaje de colaboradores justifican un viaje regional dedicado; como los 90 años de Glass se celebran en muchos lugares, ésta es una fecha central dentro de un aniversario más amplio, no la única oportunidad posible.

events.subtitle: 70th birthday + Carnegie Hall headlining debut
events.factual_description: Carnegie Hall presents Billy Childs in Zankel Hall on March 5, 2027, leading a quintet for his 70th-birthday celebration and his Carnegie Hall headlining debut. Carnegie's season announcement places the date 50 years after Childs first made his name with J. J. Johnson and Freddie Hubbard. The official season release does not name the other Carnegie quintet members or a showtime, so those details are left unfilled. SFJAZZ independently announces a separate Childs 70th-birthday concert on February 25, confirming that the birthday celebration is a broader 2027 thread rather than a one-off concept.

SFJAZZ supplies authoritative context on another 70th-birthday engagement. Exact Carnegie personnel beyond Childs and a stable event/ticket URL were not inferred. Repository search found no existing Billy Childs RADAR record.

en.why_it_matters: The strongest fact is not the round-number birthday by itself; it is that Childs reaches 70 by finally headlining Carnegie Hall under his own name, five decades after the J. J. Johnson and Freddie Hubbard years that launched him. His writing has always lived in the seam between jazz improvisation and chamber-scale composition, and Zankel is a particularly good room for that language. This is a milestone with musical shape, not just cake around a famous pianist.
en.trip_verdict: Actively make room for it if a New York trip overlaps. The headlining debut and birthday make Zankel a strong anchor for the night, but another 70th-birthday program is already announced at SFJAZZ and Carnegie has not yet published a unique premiere or final-performance context that would justify rebuilding the whole trip around this date.

es.why_it_matters: El dato fuerte no es el número redondo del cumpleaños por sí solo: Childs llega a los 70 encabezando por fin Carnegie Hall bajo su propio nombre, cinco décadas después de los años con J. J. Johnson y Freddie Hubbard que lo lanzaron. Su escritura siempre ha vivido entre la improvisación jazzística y una escala casi camerística, y Zankel le queda especialmente bien a ese lenguaje. Es un hito con forma musical, no sólo pastel alrededor de un pianista famoso.
es.trip_verdict: Sí le haría espacio activamente si coincide con un viaje a Nueva York. El debut como headliner y el cumpleaños hacen de Zankel una ancla fuerte para la noche, pero ya existe otra celebración de sus 70 años anunciada en SFJAZZ y Carnegie todavía no ha publicado un estreno único o contexto de última función que justifique rehacer todo el viaje alrededor de esta fecha.
